Dear Counsel,

Thank you for sending the Seller’s initial draft. We have reviewed the draft and propose the following principal revisions on behalf of the Buyer.

First, Buyer is not prepared to proceed at USD 45,000,000. Based on the information currently available and the risk allocation reflected in the draft, Buyer proposes a purchase price of USD 36,000,000.

Second, the closing provision should be revised so that closing occurs within 45 days after signing, subject to completion of Buyer’s confirmatory diligence, receipt of any required approvals, and satisfaction or waiver of customary closing conditions.

Third, the Seller representations should be expanded substantially. A single financial-statement representation is insufficient for a share purchase. We would expect customary representations covering authority, capitalization and title to shares, no conflicts, compliance with law, absence of undisclosed liabilities, taxes, material contracts, litigation, employees and benefits, IP, data/privacy matters, and absence of a material adverse change.

Fourth, the agreement should include a customary indemnity package, including indemnification for breaches of representations and covenants and pre-closing tax matters, supported by a 10% escrow or holdback for at least 18 months.

Finally, the confidentiality provision should include standard exceptions for disclosures to representatives, financing sources, regulators, and disclosures required by law.

Please let us know if you would like us to turn a mark-up reflecting these points.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 42,500,000 for the Shares at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur no later than 45 days after signing, subject to receipt of any required regulatory or third-party approvals and satisfaction or waiver of the closing conditions expressly set forth in this Agreement. Buyer’s confirmatory diligence shall proceed promptly and in good faith prior to Closing, but completion of such diligence shall not constitute an independent condition to Closing except to the extent expressly provided herein.

3. Representations. The Seller represents that: (a) it has authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (b) the Seller owns good and valid title to the Shares, free and clear of liens other than restrictions arising under applicable securities laws; (c) execution and performance of this Agreement do not conflict with the Seller’s organizational documents or any material agreement binding on the Seller; (d) to the Seller’s knowledge, the Company is in material compliance with applicable laws; (e) the financial statements delivered to Buyer were prepared in good faith and fairly present in all material respects the financial position of the Company for the periods presented; (f) to the Seller’s knowledge, there are no material undisclosed liabilities outside the ordinary course of business; (g) to the Seller’s knowledge, the Company has timely filed material tax returns and paid material taxes due; (h) the material contracts made available to Buyer are true and complete in all material respects; (i) to the Seller’s knowledge, there is no material litigation pending against the Company; (j) to the Seller’s knowledge, the Company is in material compliance with applicable employment and benefits laws; (k) to the Seller’s knowledge, the Company owns or has rights to use the intellectual property material to its business; (l) to the Seller’s knowledge, the Company is in material compliance with applicable data protection and privacy laws; and (m) since the date of the most recent financial statements made available to Buyer, there has not been a material adverse change in the business of the Company, taken as a whole.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement and all non-public information exchanged in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby are confidential; provided that either party may disclose such information to its representatives, financing sources, regulators, and other persons with a need to know in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby, or as required by applicable law, regulation, legal process, or stock exchange requirement, in each case subject to customary confidentiality safeguards to the extent reasonably practicable.

5. Closing Deliverables. At Closing, Seller shall deliver customary instruments of transfer evidencing transfer of good title to the Shares, officer certificates confirming satisfaction of Seller’s closing conditions, and, to the extent applicable and reasonably requested, good standing certificates and resignation documentation for directors or officers designated by Buyer prior to Closing. Buyer shall deliver the Purchase Price and customary officer certificates confirming satisfaction of Buyer’s closing conditions.

6. Indemnification. Following Closing, Seller shall indemnify Buyer for losses arising from breaches of Seller’s representations and covenants and for pre-Closing taxes of the Company, subject to customary limitations, exclusions, and mitigation obligations. Seller’s aggregate liability for non-fundamental representation claims shall not exceed 5% of the Purchase Price, and no claim for breach of non-fundamental representations may be brought after the date that is 12 months following Closing. At Closing, 5% of the Purchase Price shall be deposited into escrow for 12 months solely to secure Seller’s indemnification obligations for non-fundamental representation claims, with any undisputed balance released to Seller at the end of such period.

receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for the revised draft. Seller’s movement on timing and the expansion of the representation package are appreciated. We are aligned on a number of structural points, but several issues remain important to Buyer given the limited post-signing diligence window and the qualifications in the revised representations.

Buyer can proceed on the basis of a purchase price of USD 40,000,000, subject to the following revisions:

1. Closing / diligence. Buyer can accept a 45-day outside closing period, but the agreement should include a limited condition that, prior to Closing, Buyer has not identified a material inaccuracy in the materials provided or any matter that would reasonably be expected to constitute a Material Adverse Effect. Buyer is not seeking an open-ended diligence out, but it cannot be required to close if confirmatory diligence reveals a material problem.

2. Seller representations. The expanded representations are helpful, but several core reps should not be knowledge-qualified. In particular, authority, title to shares, no-conflict, financial statements, taxes, material contracts, and undisclosed liabilities should be given on an unqualified basis, subject to appropriate materiality qualifiers where customary.

3. Indemnity / escrow. The proposed 5% escrow for 12 months is too narrow relative to the representation package and the reduced diligence protection. Buyer proposes a 7.5% escrow for 15 months. As an alternative, Buyer would consider a 5% escrow if Seller’s aggregate cap for non-fundamental representation claims is increased to 7.5% of the purchase price, with direct recourse to Seller above the escrow.

4. Fundamental claims, taxes and fraud. The agreement should expressly provide that fundamental representations, pre-Closing taxes, and fraud are not subject to the non-fundamental cap or 12-month survival period. Fundamental representations should include, at minimum, authority, title/ownership of the shares, capitalization/valid issuance to the extent applicable, and broker fees.

If Seller can accept the USD 40,000,000 price and the targeted protections above, Buyer believes the parties should be well positioned to move promptly to signing.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
